*Introduction*:
The Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (Special Component Scheme(scp)) was being implemented from the year 1982-83 to increase the income of Scheduled Caste / New-Buddhist farmers and improve their standard of living. Since the said scheme has been implemented for a long period of time, the GOVERNMENT OF MAHARASHTRA has decided to implement the Special Component Scheme for Scheduled Caste / Neo-Buddhist farmers since 1982-83 and the recommendations of the Agriculture Commissionerate dated 27/04/2016 on the report dated 19/04/2016 and special component scheme the announced by the Hon'ble Minister (Finance). Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Krishi Swavalamban Yojana is not being implemented separately, but the current special component scheme, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Krishi Swavalamban Yojana, is being implemented from 2016-17 as per the changed criteria, taking into account the needs of the changed situation and maintaining soil moisture.
Also, the government has approved the amendment in the financial criteria and inclusion of new components under the said scheme as per the government decision dated 01 October, 2024.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    beneficiary Selection criteria are as follows
1.  Scheme is only for Scheduled Caste/ Nav Baudha farmers.
2.  Scheme is implemented in all districts of Maharashtra (Except Mumbai districts).
3. At field level  scheme is under Implementation by department of Agriculture, Zilha Parishad.
4. Funds are released from Social Justice Department to concerned  District Collector and then made available to concern Zilha Parishad.
5. Application ,Selection of beneficiaries upto payment of subsidy all process are done through MAHADBT Portal through online system.                                                                  "

*Benefits*:
Benefit provided on subsidy basis as per the norms of components, through online system. The said scheme shall be implemented in the financial year 2025-26 as follows. In the said scheme, grants shall be admissible for the following components in the year 2025-26 up to the maximum limit of the amount mentioned below.
1. For New Irrigation- Well Maximum subsidy ammount limit is Rs.4,00,000/ - is admissible.
2. For Old Well Repair - Maximum subsidy ammount limit is 1,00,000/- is admissible
3. Plastic Lining of Farm Ponds-Grant shall be admissible up to 90% of the amount calculated as per the prevailing financial parameters of the National Horticulture Mission Guideline and the size of the farm pond or actual cost or Rs. 2,00,000/- whichever is less is admissible.
4.Inwell Boring- Maximum subsidy ammount limit is 40,000/- is admissible
5. Electricity Connection-Maximum subsidy ammount limit is Amount 20,000/- or actual paid amount whichever is less is admissible.
6. Pump Set (Diesel/Electric)(Diesel Engine - New Item) For pump sets up to 10 HP capacity, grant shall be admissible up to 90% of the prevailing financial parameters or actual cost or Rs. 40,000/- whichever is less is admissible.
7. Grant Solar pump (instead of electrical connection and pump set)- Maximum subsidy will be admissible up to 90% of the prevailing financial criteria or actual expenditure incurred or Rs. 50,000/- whichever is less is admissible.
8. HDPE/PVC Pipe (New Item)- Under the Food and Nutrition Security Scheme - Food Crops Scheme, subsidy of 100% of the prevailing economic standard or actual cost incurred per meter or Rs. 50,000/- whichever is less will be admissible.
9.1 For Micro irrigation system Under Sprinkler Irrigation Set (Supplementary Grant) 9.1.1) Under the Per Drop More Crop Scheme, (1) 55% for small/very small landholders + 25% from the Chief Minister's Sustainable Irrigation Scheme + 10% from Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Krishi Swavalamban Yojana and9.1.2) 45% for large landholders + 30% from the Chief Minister's Sustainable Irrigation Scheme + 15% from Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Krishi Swavalamban Yojana or Rs. 47,000/- whichever is less will be admissible as subsidy. (Total subsidy limit of 90 percent) is admissible
9.2 For Drip Irrigation Set Supplementary Grant 9.2.1 ) Under the Per Drop More Crop Scheme, (1) 55% for small/very small landholders + 25% from the Chief Minister's Sustainable Irrigation Scheme + 10% from Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Krishi Swavalamban Yojana and 9.2.2) 45% for large landholders + 30% from the Chief Minister's Sustainable Irrigation Scheme + 15% from Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Krishi Swavalamban Yojana or Rs. 97,000/- whichever is less will be admissible as subsidy.(Total subsidy limit of 90 percent) is admissible
10. Farm Machinery (bullock-drawn/tractor-drawn implements) (New item)maximum subsidy limit is 50,000/- is admissible
11. Backyard / Kitchen Garden (New Item) maximum subsidy limit is 50,000/- is admissible .

*Eligibility*:
1. Scheme is only for Scheduled Tribe farmers. Caste  certificate is essential.
2. Land holding limit is 0.20 ha. to  6.00 ha.(for benefit of New well component minimum 0.40 ha. land essential)
3.1 It will be mandatory for the beneficiary to be a farmer belonging to the Scheduled Caste / Neo-Buddhist category.
3.2 The farmer must have a caste certificate issued by the competent authority.
3.3 Farmers residing the Outside the Nagar Panchayat, Nagarpalika and Mahanagarpalika is necessary to have 7/12 certificate and 8A extract of land tenure in the name of the farmer. ( Outside the Nagar Panchayat, Nagarpalika and Mahanagarpalika area (Reference Government Letter No. Sankirna- 2017/Pr.No.142/3A, dated 24 April 2018))
3.4 The beneficiaries must have their own Aadhaar link active bank account .
3.5 The beneficiaries below the poverty line will be given  first priority.
3.6 The beneficiary farmer must have a minimum of 0.40 hectares and a maximum of 6 hectares of agricultural land. If the beneficiary's land is in a remote and fragmented area and two or more beneficiaries with less than 0.40 hectares of land come together and their combined land is at least 0.40 hectares, then if they sign an agreement, they will be eligible for the benefit of the scheme. Similarly, the condition of maximum 6.0 hectares of land will not be applicable to the beneficiaries below the poverty line.
3.7 Once the full benefit of the relevant scheme is taken, the benefit of this scheme will not be payable to the same beneficiary or family for the next five years. The beneficiary who has taken the benefit of the new well component will be eligible for the benefit of the old well repair component after 20 years.
If the benefit has been given under the Special Component Scheme for similar agricultural development schemes and the scheme implemented from the funds made available under the SCA of the Central Government and Article 275 (A) of the Constitution, the benefit provided under this scheme will not be admissible.

*Required Documents*:
1. Caste Certificate of SC category issued by compitant authority
2. current 7/12 report having Land holding limit is 0.20 ha. to 6.00 ha.(for benefit of New well component minimum 0.40 ha. land essential) within the period of
3 months 3.GSDA Certificates
4. There is no income limit for this scheme

*Application Process*:
Application is to done online on Mahadbt portal as follows
1. Applications from farmers are being invited for the said scheme on the Maha-DBT portal website mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in/farmer/login /login and the applications received within the limit of lakhs received by the concerned talukas / blocks will be selected online on a first come, first served basis (fcfs). After selection, all the proceedings up to the payment of subsidy to the beneficiaries should be done online. In this regard, proceedings from acceptance of application to payment of subsidy to the beneficiaries should be done as mentioned in the referenced government decision dated 04/11/2020.
2. The Agricultural Officer (Agriculture), P.S., should conduct a site inspection of the area of the beneficiary selected for the new well and old well repair on a first come, first served basis and check the technical feasibility. After the inspection, if the location of the beneficiary's new well and the proposal for repair of the old well of the beneficiary is technically suitable, the Agricultural Development Officer should approve the budget for this matter and give prior approval to the proposals of the concerned beneficiary within a maximum of 30 days after uploading the documents. Similarly, the selection of the beneficiaries whose proposals are found to be technically unsuitable during the site inspection should be cancelled.
3. Beneficiaries selected for other matters other than new well and old well repair under the scheme should be given prior approval within a maximum of 30 days after uploading the documents and they should be given the benefit of the scheme in the current financial year 2025-26 itself.
4. The prior approval of the beneficiaries who do not implement the matters under the scheme within the prescribed period should be cancelled.
5. While selecting individual beneficiary, priority will be given to women and disabled beneficiaries. Out of the total sanctioned funds, 5 percent of the funds should be given priority to be spent on disabled beneficiaries and 30 percent of the funds should be spent on women beneficiaries.
6. As per the demand of the final selected beneficiaries as per the target of the taluka & district, a draft plan of the district should be prepared within 7 days as per Appendix No. 1, component-wise and beneficiary-wise. The responsibility of preparing the draft plan will be the responsibility of the Agricultural Development Officer.

## 3. Scheme Information

State

National Mission on Edible Oils  Oilseeds

*Main Component*:
1) Purchase of Breeder Seed

6) Flexi Component

*Sub Component*:
1) Puchase of Breeder Seed- Soybean, Groundnut,  Mustard, Sanflower, Safflower, Niger
2) Crop Demonstration & Certified Seed Distribution, Soil sample testing, Krishi Mapper Registration, Farmer training & Farmer field school- Soybean, Groundnut,  Mustard, Sanflower, Safflower, Niger
2) Post Harvest Technology - Oil extraction Unit
3) Flexi component - Godown construction & Workshop

*Introduction*:
National Mission on Oilseed and Oil Palm (NMOOP) was launched by Government of India in year 2014-15. In 2018-19 GoI has merged NMOOP with NFSM as NFSM (OS&OP).  Afterwards, from the year 2022-23, NFSM (OS & OP) subsumed as National Mission On Edible Oil (NMEO) and till 2024-25, the following three missions were under this mission. 1) Mission No. 1: Oilseeds Crops 2) Mission No. 3: Tree Oilseeds Crops 3) TRFA (Oilseeds).
         The Central Government has approved a new Mission called National Mission on Edible Oil Oilseeds for the years 2024-25 to 2030-31. This has been done to promote the production of oilseed crops with primary focus on mustard, groundnut and soybean and to focus on secondary oilseeds and tree-borne oilseeds (TBO) along with other oilseed crops. Secondary Vegetable Oil Sub-mission is also part of the National Mission on Edible Oil Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) mission and has been included in it, which mainly includes oil extraction from secondary sources like cottonseed, rice bran and tree-borne oilseeds (TBO). Under this mission, 27 districts of Maharashtra have been selected for soybean, groundnut, safflower, mustard, Niger, sunflower and sesame. The mission will be implemented through Value Chain Cluster (VCC) and for this, a farmer producer company/cooperative/public or private organization will be selected as the Value Chain Partner (VCP) for each cluster. At the district level, the Value Chain Partners (VCPs) will be selected by the District Executive Committee (DEC).
        While implementing the components under the scheme in the year 2025-26, while selecting beneficiaries, the following category wise allocation should be made: General 74.80%, Scheduled Castes 16.60%, Scheduled Tribes 8.60%. Also, preference should be given to women and disabled beneficiaries.

*Benefits*:
1.Adoption of new technologies: Utilization of available and emerging innovations and technologies to bridge the production gap.
2. Acceleration of improved seed dissemination: Dissemination of improved seed varieties (distributed in the last five years) and technology in selected clusters.
3. Expansion: Promotion of oilseed cultivation on fallow land and promotion of intercropping through demonstrations.
4. Availability of improved seeds: Elimination of deficiencies in seed production and distribution systems to ensure availability of quality seeds.
5. Linkage to marketing system: Linking oilseed farmers and Value Chain Partners (VCPs) to marketing system and processing industries.
6. Support for oil production and collection from secondary oilseeds: Increasing production of secondary oilseeds and tree-borne oilseeds (TBOs) in particular.

*Eligibility*:
1. For Demonstration -  Group of farmer
2. For Certified Seed Distribution - Individual farmer in VCC
3. for Post harvest technology & Godown  - Group i.e. FPO / FPC / Co-operatives etc.

*Required Documents*:

2. For Farmer group - Group register with any Govt. organization before March, 2024

*Application Process*:
1. For Demonstration & Certified Seed Distribution -  Selection of Applicant through MahaDBT portal
2. for Post harvest technology & Godown  - Selection of Applicant through DOSM.

Risk covered -  Crop cutting base average yield reduction in comparison to threshhold yield for that insurance unit( Revenue circle)

*Introduction*:
1. The scheme is applicable for notified crops in a notified area (revenue circle). All farmers including share-croppers, tenant farmers growing notified crops in the notified area.
2. The scheme is optional for both loanee as well as non-loanee  farmers.
3. Under this scheme, the indemnity level is  fixed as 70 % for all notified crops.
4. Threshold yield  is determined by taking into account the average average yield  of the  best five years from past 7 years multiplied by  indemnity level
5. The scheme is implemented on beed pattern (80:110) where Insurance companies claim liability is up to 110 %  of the gross premium  or 110% of the burn cost whichever is higher for the given cluster in given season . question: मिरचीतील चुरडा-मुरडा (Leaf Curl) कशामुळे होतो आणि तो कसा दुरुस्त करावा?
answer:
मिरचीतील चुरडा-मुरडा हा विषाणूजन्य रोग आहे, जो मुख्यतः पाने मुरडणे, पाने बारीक होणे आणि पानांचा गुच्छ तयार होणे अशी लक्षणे देतो.

**कारणे:**
- हा रोग पांढरी माशी या रसशोषक कीटकाद्वारे प्रसारित होतो; पांढरी माशी पानाच्या खालच्या भागातून व नवत्यातून रस शोषते आणि त्यामुळे पानाचा आकार बदलतो तसेच चुरडा-मुरडाचा प्रसार वाढतो?
- काही ठिकाणी इतर रसशोषक किडींमुळे (मापकीड, फुलकिडे, अळ्या) रोगाचा प्रसार होऊ शकतो असे नमूद आहे?

**नियंत्रण:**
- कडुलिंबाचे तेल ५% दर १० दिवसांनी फवारणी केल्याने प्रकोप कमी करण्यास मदत होते?
- पांढरी माशी नियंत्रणासाठी फेनप्रोपाथ्रिन ३० ई.सी. ३.५ मि.ली. किंवा पायरीप्रॉक्सीफेन ५% + फेनप्रोपाथ्रिन १५% ई.सी. १० मि.ली. हे दहा लिटर पाण्यात मिसळून फवारणी करावी?
- मापकीड नियंत्रणासाठी इमिडाक्लोप्रिड १७.८% एस.एल. ५ मि.ली./दहा लिटर पाणी आणि फुलकिडे नियंत्रणासाठी फिप्रोनिल ५ एस.सी. २० मि.ली. फवारणी उपलब्ध दस्तऐवजांत दिली आहे?

**स्रोत: कृषी दस्तऐवज (व्ही.एन.एम.के.व्ही., परभणी), एम.पी.के.व्ही. कृषी दर्शनी, डॉ. पंजाबराव देशमुख कृषी विद्यापीठ, कृषी व्ही.एन.एम.ए.यू.)**

तुमच्या बागेत सध्या पांढरी माशी जास्त दिसते का, की मापकीड/फुलकिडे हीच जास्त आहे??

answer:
थीट पेरणी झालेल्या भातात बाजूच्या फांद्या वाढणे (बुशनिंग) चांगले करायचे असेल तर सुरूवातीला माती सतत ओली ठेवणे, उचलताना रोप साधे व मूळ तुटणार नाही अशा प्रकारे लावणे आणि आंतरमशागतने तण वेळेत काढणे हे मुख्य काम आहे.

**पाणी व्यवस्थापन:**  
- लागवडीनंतरच्या सुरुवातीच्या टप्प्यात नियंत्रित पाणी द्यावे म्हणजे माती सतत ओली राहील.  
- खूप जास्त पाणी/अतिद्रावस्थिती टाळावी.

**लागवड पद्धत:**  
- रोपे कमी वयाची (८ ते १५ दिवस) असताना उचलावीत.  
- रोपे ऊतकधारक मूळ तुटल्याशिवाय, थोडी खोल न करता थेट व सोप्या पद्धतीने लावावीत; यामुळे रोप लवकर घट्ट होते आणि बाजूच्या फांद्या वाढण्यास मदत होते.

**आंतरमशागत व तण नियंत्रण:**  
- लागवडीनंतर पहिल्या टप्प्यात तणांचा प्रादुर्भाव जास्त होतो, त्यामुळे ताशी गुर्म किंवा कोनो विडरने वारंवार तण काढणे किंवा हाताने निंदन करावे.  
- लागवडीनंतर ३ दिवसांनी ब्युटाक्लोर ५० ई.सी. ३.७५ ली. + पाणी ५०० ली. प्रति हेक्टर असे फवारणीसह तण नियंत्रण करावे.  
- लागवडीनंतर ३० दिवसांनी कोनो विडरने आंतरमशागत करावी.

Turmeric [हळद] Processing [प्रक्रिया] Technology

Boiling Turmeric [हळद]: The turmeric [हळद] that is dug out of the field [शेत] cannot be used for our daily use. It has to be boiled and processed before use. Turmeric [हळद] is traditionally boiled in an iron [लोह] pan (kadai). These pans are of varying capacities in different regions. Generally, there are pans ranging from two quintals of fresh turmeric [हळद] capacity to pans that can hold 8 to 10 quintals of turmeric [हळद].

In these pans, the turmeric [हळद] is filled, and the top is closed by covering it with turmeric [हळद] foliage and gunny sacks, and the turmeric [हळद] is boiled. In some places, the turmeric [हळद] is filled in a semicircular way over the pan, and the top is sealed by covering it with foliage and mud plaster. The more turmeric [हळद] is filled in the pan while boiling, the longer it will take for the turmeric [हळद] to boil. In this method, the turmeric [हळद] near the bottom of the pan boils more. Sometimes it gets burnt. Such turmeric [हळद] is called iron [लोह] turmeric [हळद]. There is a possibility that the turmeric [हळद] in the upper part remains raw because the lid of the pan is not completely airtight. Such turmeric [हळद] does not get a good shine. While polishing [पॉलिश करणे], its pieces fly off. As a result, such goods do not get a good market price [बाजार भाव]. For this, if turmeric [हळद] is to be boiled in a pan, put water on the turmeric [हळद] layer [अंडी देणारी कोंबडी] so that 5 to 8 cm of water remains on it, and then boil it by covering it with turmeric [हळद] foliage and gunny sacks, so that the turmeric [हळद] boils properly and in less time and with less fuel.

Supportive treatment [उपचार] is advisable, particularly in valuable animals, and may include the use of anti-inflammatory drugs, corticosteroids, and fluid therapy. Blood [रक्त] transfusions may be lifesaving in very anemic animals.

Tick Control

Tick control, via acaricides or management [व्यवस्थापन] practices, can be useful in reducing tick burdens, which can lower transmission rates. However, this can lead to naive cattle [गाय वर्ग] populations, with consequent risk of outbreaks of disease [रोग] should tick populations increase. Chemical tick control cannot be relied upon to prevent transmission of *Babesia*, and outbreaks often occur after introduction of susceptible cattle [गाय वर्ग] to endemic areas despite acaricide use. Acaricide resistance is also an increasing problem. However, acaricidal tick control before moving animals from tickinfested areas is useful to prevent the introduction of ticks and babesiosis to tick-free areas.

Eradication of the tick vector is rarely feasible on individual premises but may work on a regional level in well-coordinated programs.

Using Resistant Breeds

*Bos indicus*based breeds are commonly used to minimize production [उत्पादन] losses associated with ticks and babesiosis.

Turmeric [हळद]

Season and Planting Method: Turmeric [हळद] should be planted from Akshaya Tritiya, i.e., the last week of April, to May. At the latest, turmeric [हळद] should be planted in the first fortnight of June. Delaying the planting of turmeric [हळद] hurts its yield [उत्पादन].

Pre-cultivation: Turmeric [हळद] is a rhizome [कंद] that grows in the soil [माती]. Therefore, the looser the soil [माती], the better the turmeric [हळद] production [उत्पादन]. For this, the land should be ploughed 2-3 times in both directions (vertically and horizontally) to a depth of 18 to 22 cm. The first ploughing [नांगरणी] should be done in March. The soil [माती] should be allowed to heat in the sun for 15-20 days. After that, the second ploughing [नांगरणी] should be done, and clods should be broken. 25 to 40 tons of welldecomposed farmyard manure [शेणखत] should be mixed into the soil [माती]. After giving one or two harrowing [वखरणी] passes, the remains of other crops and weeds [तण] should be removed from the land to make it clean. In some places, sheep [मेंढी] are also penned (for manure [खत]).

Planting Method: Turmeric [हळद] is planted in two methods:

\* Ridge and Furrow [सरी व वरंबा] Method: To plant turmeric [हळद] using this method, furrows should be made at a distance of 75 cm. On both sides of the furrow [सरी], planting should be done at a distance of 30 cm between two sets of rhizomes (gaudy).

\* Broad Bed Method: If planting is to be done using this method, furrows should be made at a distance of 1.5 m, meaning that a raised bed [उंच वाफे] of 90 cm to 1 meter is created between two furrows. On this raised bed [उंच वाफे] or broad bed, planting is done keeping a distance of 30 cm between two rows and two plants. However, the land must be level in this method. Therefore, the water released into the beds can be provided properly, which helps in good production [उत्पादन]. In the broad bed method, higher yields can be obtained in some places by constructing field [शेत] bunds.

**Broad Bed and Furrow [रुंद वाफे व सरी] Method:**

The Broad Bed and Furrow [रुंद वाफे व सरी] (BBF) method is useful from the point of view of water conservation [पाण्याचे संवर्धन] as well as drainage of excess water in heavy soils. Furrows are taken on both sides of the ridge [वरंबा] according to the planning that two rows of crops with more distance or 3 to 4 rows of crops with less distance will come on the ridge [वरंबा]. The furrows should be given a slope of 0.1 to 0.3 percent. Sowing [पेरणी] or planting should be done in a row on the ridge [वरंबा].

All three tasks of making broad beds of required width, giving fertilizers, and sowing [पेरणी] can be done simultaneously at one time with the help of BBF machine. In soybean [सोयाबीन] crop [पीक], the machine should be operated by keeping the forks of the BBF machine at a distance of 150 cm. In this, a broad ridge [वरंबा] of 120 cm distance is formed and 4 rows of soybean [सोयाबीन] crop [पीक] can be taken on it at a distance of 30 cm. In BBF method (Broad Bed Furrow [रुंद बेड आणि सरी] method) in Bt Cotton [बीटी कापूस], planting can be done in 2 ways. In the first type, a broad bed of 90 cm width should be prepared by operating the BBF machine by keeping the forks of the BBF machine at a distance of 120 cm and cotton [कापूस] should be planted on it at 120 x 45 cm. In the second type, if the distance between the two forks of the BBF machine is kept at 180 cm and the machine is operated, a ridge [वरंबा] of 150 cm width is formed and two rows should be planted on one broad ridge [वरंबा] (bed) at a distance of 120 cm and the distance between the two seeds / plants should be kept at 60 cm. In this, planting should be done in a paired row method at 120-60-120 cm.

answer:

- एफ.एम.डी.: पहिले लसीकरण वयाच्या ३ महिन्यांनी, मात्रा ३ मि.ली. (त्वचेखाली), प्रतिकारशक्ती १ वर्ष  
- ब्लॅक क्वार्टर: पहिले लसीकरण वयाच्या ६ महिन्यांनी, मात्रा ५ मि.ली. (त्वचेखाली), प्रतिकारशक्ती ६ महिना ते १ वर्ष  
- हेमोरॅजिक सप्टिसीमिया: पहिले लसीकरण वयाच्या ६ महिन्यांनी, मात्रा ५ मि.ली. (त्वचेखाली), प्रतिकारशक्ती ६ महिना ते १ वर्ष  
- अँथ्रॅक्स: पहिले लसीकरण वयाच्या ६ महिन्यांनी, मात्रा १ मि.ली. (त्वचेखाली), प्रतिकारशक्ती १ वर्ष  
- ब्रुकॅला (S-19): फक्त गाय वर्गातील वासरूंना वय ४–८ महिने असतानाच, मात्रा ५ मि.ली. (त्वचेखाली)

question: काढणीनंतर बटाट्याची सुरक्षित साठवणूक कशी करावी?
answer:
काढणीनंतर बटाट्याची सुरक्षित साठवणूक करायची असेल तर आधी मारलेले, भेगा पडलेले आणि दाबलेले कंद वेगळे करून स्वच्छ, हवेशीर व कोमट जागेत काही दिवस ठेवावेत; त्यानंतर प्रतवारी करून प्लास्टिक क्रेटमध्ये भरून थंड खोलीत (किंवा शेत-आधारित जीरो एनर्जी थंड खोलीत) साठवावे?

**साठवण:**
- काढणीनंतर मारलेले, भेगा पडलेले, दाबलेले कंद वेगळे करा
- प्रतवारी केलेल्या कंदांची प्लास्टिक क्रेटमध्ये भरणी करा
- क्रेट थंड खोलीत ठेवून वर झाकण घाला
- थंड खोलीच्या बाहेरील बाजूस पाण्याचा फवारणी दररोज सकाळ-संध्याकाळ दोन वेळा करा

**थंड खोलीतील तापमान व आर्द्रता:**
- उन्हाळ्यात थंड खोलीचे तापमान बाह्य तापमानापेक्षा १५ ते १८ से.मी. ने कमी होते

9.2.3 Preservation of meat [मांस]

 The primary objective is to inhibit microbial spoilage and arrest physio-chemical process which brings about deterioration in quality. Methods used for preservation are as follows

1. Refrigeration : Meat [मांस] can be stored at 10 to 40 C with relative humidity [सापेक्ष आर्द्रता] of 80-85% for about a week. Crushed ice or mechanical refrigeration are generally used for chilling or cold storage [शीतगृह].

2. Freezing : Meat [मांस] can be frozen in air or liquid or refrigerated plates. Ideally, only chilled carcasses should be frozen.

a. Slow freezing : Still air, the method generally used in home freezer or small freezing operation.

b. Quick [नखाचा रक्तवाहिनी असलेला भाग] freezing : Air blast [करपा] system used in commercial operation. Meat [मांस] stored at -200 C for 12, 15, 18 months with excellent, good and satisfactory quality, respectively.

3. Curing and smoking : These are closely interrelated and often practiced together. Curing is the process of salting meat [मांस] along with one or more of the glutamates, ascorbic acid, acetic acid and phosphate. Cured chicken are smoked in a smoke chamber maintained at 40- 450 C and 30-35% relative humidity [सापेक्ष आर्द्रता] for about 4 hours. The smoking process imparts a characteristic flavour and stable colour to the cured product and helps in preservation. Cured chicken could be stored for 4 and 14 days at ambient (260 C) and refrigeration (4-50 C) temperature [तापमान], respectively while cured and smoked chicken for 14 and 30 days under the corresponding storage conditions [साठवणूक मापदंड].

4. Dehydration [निर्जलीकरण] : Conventional hot air, drum, spray and freeze drying [गोठवून सुकवणे] are the methods used to remove moisture from poultry [कुक्कुट] meat [मांस]. Generally, cooked meat [मांस] is dehydrated. Dehydrated product is a porous mass with original shape and size which can remain stable up to 1 year under ambient condition when packed in tins under nitrogen [नत्र].

\* Elephant Foot Yam [सुरण / जिमीकंद]: For the control of these pests and diseases, spray imidacloprid (17.8 SL) at 1 ml and carbendazim at 1 gram [हरभरा] per 1 litre of water as soon as the infestation is seen when the wind [वारा] is calm. Scale insects are also seen to infest the tubers in the field [शेत] as well as in storage [साठवण]. To control them, dip the tubers in the solution of imidacloprid insecticide [कीटकनाशक] before planting and then plant. Use scale-insect [कीटक]-free tuber [कंद] seeds for planting. Use neem cake [कडुलिंबाचा पेंढ] in the pit at the time of planting. Nematodes are seen to infest the tubers. To control them, intercrop marigolds on both sides of the furrow [सरी] or use neem cake [कडुलिंबाचा पेंढ] or carbofuran [कार्बोफ्युरान] 3 G.

\* Lesser Yam: Leaf spot disease [पानांवरील ठिपक्यांचा रोग] is sometimes seen. Take integrated disease control [रोग नियंत्रण] measures to control it. This includes crop rotation [पीक फेरपालट], using disease [रोग]-free seeds, and spraying [फवारणी] dithane M-45 or bavistin fungicide [बुरशीनाशक] immediately after the disease [रोग] symptoms [लक्षणे] appear.

\* Air Potato [बटाटा]: If the environment is conducive to pests, after the *karanda* are formed on the vine, fruit-boring caterpillars are seen to infest. For this, spraying [फवारणी] imidacloprid (17.8 SL) at 1 ml per 1 litre of water is sufficient.

**Zero Energy Based Cold Room for Storing Fruits and Vegetables**

To avoid spoilage of fruits and vegetables, the producer can build a cold room in his field [शेत] for storage [साठवण] himself. It is called a zero energy based cold room. Because no kind of mechanical, chemical and electrical energy is required while storing fruits and vegetables in this cold room. This cold room is very easy to build and is economically cheap.

**How to build a cold room**

The cold room is designed on the principle of creating cooling by evaporation. The cold room can be made from easily available bricks, sand, bamboo [बांबू], vala and wasted sacks. The design of this cold room is like a small tank. Lay the bottom part of the chamber with a layer [अंडी देणारी कोंबडी] of bricks. Fill fine sand in the space between the two bricks. Then construct two walls of bricks and keep the distance between the two walls 7.5 cm. The space between the two walls should also be filled with sand. In this way, prepare a tank with the help of sand and bricks. To cover this, prepare a cover by spreading vala on the sack with the help of bamboo [बांबू] and tying it with twine. If vala is not available, use coconut [नारळ] leaves. In this way the cold room is built and ready. The cold room should preferably be built under a tree or under a roof. Sprinkle water on the outside of the walls of the cold room twice a day, every morning and evening, and wet the walls well. In places where there is a shortage of water, keep a plastic drum at some distance from the cold room at a certain height and fill the drum with water. Connect a pipe to the drum and place the pipe on the sand on the top side of the cold room and attach small nozzles of the drip kit to it, which saves water.

## **Cold Storage [शीतगृह] of Fruits and Vegetables**

The total production [उत्पादन] of fruits and vegetables in our country is approximately more than 351.92 million tons. However, due to improper handling after harvesting [कापणी], 20 to 30% of the production [उत्पादन] is wasted every year. Among them, fruits and vegetables are spoiled on a large scale due to the lack of proper storage [साठवण] facilities. Fruits and vegetables are seasonal and they are perishable. Due to high temperature [तापमान] after harvesting [कापणी] and 5 to 10% water evaporation from the vegetables, they start drying [वाळवणे]. Their freshness and attractiveness disappear. The main purpose of storage [साठवण] is to increase the shelf life [टिकाऊपणा] of fruits and vegetables. This makes fruits and vegetables available to the customer for a long time. During the season, a huge amount of fruits and vegetables arrive in the market at the same time. At that time, the prices collapse and the producer has to suffer a loss. However, if the goods can be stored in this situation, then the producer can bring his goods for sale when he starts getting a good price in the market. Therefore, it is very important to store fruits and vegetables to stop price fluctuations and to avoid wastage.

**How to store?**

After harvesting [कापणी], some internal biological and chemical processes continue uninterruptedly in fruits and vegetables. These processes include evaporation, ripening, etc. These processes are related to the storage [साठवण] temperature [तापमान]. At low temperatures, the speed of these processes slows down. Fruits and vegetables are spoiled due to the infestation of microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव]. Each fruit and vegetable has to be stored in cold storage [शीतगृह] at a specific temperature [तापमान] and specific relative humidity [सापेक्ष आर्द्रता] as per their needs. This increases the life of fruits and vegetables. question: खर्च आणि नफा यातील बदल शेतावर करून दाखवतात का?
answer:
खर्च आणि नफा यातील बदल शेतावर करून दाखवायचे असेल तर शेतकऱ्याला नियमित नोंदी ठेवणे हेच व्यावहारिक उपाय आहे; त्यामुळे कोणत्याही वेळी व्यवसायाची स्थिती, फायदा की तोटा हा ठरवता येतो.

**नोंद ठेवण्याची पद्धत:**
- नोंदी ही रोजच्या शेती क्रियेतील महत्त्वाचा भाग असून मूल्यांकन व आर्थिक तपासणीसाठी उपयोगी पडते
- नोंदींमधून उत्पादन खर्च ठरवता येतो (उदा. दुग्धव्यवसायात दूध उत्पादनाचा खर्च)
- नोंदींचा वापर करून कोणत्याही वेळी वर्षभरात फायदेशीरता की तोटा हा ठरवता येतो

**नोंदी कशा ठेवू (पर्याय):**
- कागदोपत्री/हाताने: नोटबुक, लॉगबुक किंवा छापलेले फॉर्म
- इलेक्ट्रॉनिक: एक्सेलसारखी स्प्रेडशीट (घटनांची माहिती व्यवस्थित ठेवता येते, रुझार पाहणे सोपे)
- शेती व्यवस्थापन सॉफ्टवेअर: नोंदी केंद्रित ठिकाणी, अद्ययावत अपडेट्स, अहवाल/विश्लेषण सुविधा

**नोंदीत नेहमी काय लिहायचे (माहिती साधारण):**
- सिंचन खर्च, पीक संरक्षण (कीटकनाशके/तणनाशके), अप्रत्यक्ष खर्च, जैव खते, सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये, पीक विमा, औजार घटकांवरील हाले/खरेदी, जमीनभाडे, कर व महसूल इत्यादी

**स्रोत: जनावर विज्ञान व तंत्रज्ञान प्रमाण XII, उत्तम व्यवस्थापन पद्धती (सजावटी गोडपाणी मासे उत्पादन), जीवजंतु आरोग्य व पोषण विस्तार**

Collect tissue samples from necropsied animals, including lymph nodes, spleen, lungs, and heart, for virus isolation [अलग ठेवणे] and histopathology [ऊतक रोगशास्त्र]. Samples should be collected in sterile VTM/PBS for PCR [पीसीआर] and virus isolation [अलग ठेवणे], whereas samples should be collected in 10 percent formalin for histopathology [ऊतक रोगशास्त्र]. Capture and submit Culicoides midges for virus detection to identify vector involvement in transmission. Samples should be kept cool and transported to the laboratory as soon as possible, ideally within 24- 48 hours, to preserve the integrity of the virus for accurate testing.

**STANDARD VETERINARY TREATMENT GUIDELINES FOR LIVESTOCK AND POULTRY**

Diagnosis [निदान]

Diagnosis [निदान] is based on isolation [अलग ठेवणे] and identification of *E. coli* from lesions typical of colibacillosis [कॉलिबॅसिलोसिस]. Care must be taken to avoid faecal contamination of samples. Material should be streaked on eosin-methylene blue (EMB) or MacConkey agar, as well as noninhibitory media. A presumptive diagnosis [निदान] of *E. coli* infection [संसर्ग] can be made if most of the colonies are characteristically dark with a metallic sheen on EMB agar and bright pink with a precipitate surrounding the colonies on MacConkey agar. Strains of *E. coli* can be slow or non-lactose fermenters and appear as non-lactose fermenting colonies. Multiplex PCR [पीसीआर] for 6 virulence genes of *E. coli* help to distinguish between commensal and pathogenic isolates.

Treatment [उपचार]

Antimicrobial therapy - as per the antimicrobial sensitivity test - under the supervision of the poultry [कुक्कुट] veterinarian [पशुवैद्यक] along with supportive therapy [सहायक उपचार] will reduce the losses in clinical infection [संसर्ग]. Strict withdrawal period should be followed after administration of antibiotics. Water sanitation and acidification of feed and water helps in prevention [प्रतिबंध].

Control

Proper breeder [संकरक] farm and hatchery [अंडी उबवणूक केंद्र] hygiene [स्वच्छता] and sanitization. Feed hygiene [आहार स्वच्छता] and gut health management [आरोग्य व्यवस्थापन].

Control

Proper breeder [संकरक] farm and hatchery [अंडी उबवणूक केंद्र] hygiene [स्वच्छता] and sanitization. Feed hygiene [आहार स्वच्छता] and gut health management [आरोग्य व्यवस्थापन].

Prevention [प्रतिबंध]/Biosecurity [जैवसुरक्षा]

Feed contamination with *E. coli* can be a source of infection [संसर्ग] for poultry [कुक्कुट]. Hence, it is advisable to use acidifiers (organic [सेंद्रिय] acids, pre- and pro-biotics (competitive exclusion)) and essential oils [आवश्यक तेल] as per recommended doses in the feed to maintain the gut integrity and reduce the *E. coli* contamination.

Water hygiene [स्वच्छता] includes following steps:
- Regular administration of water sanitizers such as Chlorine dioxide@0.2 ml/L
- Use of water acidifiers to reduce the pH.
- Regular removal of biofilms in the pipelines by using 10% H2 O2 .
- Ensure regular care of clean drinking water [स्वच्छ पाणी देणे] pipes.
- Rodent, insect [कीटक], and pest control [कीड नियंत्रण].
- Personal hygiene [स्वच्छता] of farm workers.
- Avoiding open defecation in farm premises.
- Regular cleaning [साफसफाई] and disinfection of poultry [कुक्कुट]

sheds can help to reduce the environmental buildup of *E. coli.*

Waste disposal in a poultry [कुक्कुट] farm is important to check further infection [संसर्ग]. Various steps include used poultry [कुक्कुट] litter [कचरा], carcasses, and other potentially contaminated farm waste should be transported and disposed of in a safe manner (deep burial, incineration or composting [खतनिर्मिती]) to prevent the direct or indirect exposure of humans, livestock [पशुधन] and wildlife to *E. coli*.

question: माझ्या शेतातील फळे आणि फुलांचे नुकसान झाले आहे. त्या नुकसानीसाठी कोणती मदत किंवा योजना उपलब्ध आहे का?
answer:
तुमच्या शेतातील फळे-फुलांचे नुकसान झाले तरी त्याच कारणानुसार मदतीचे मार्ग वेगवेगळे असतात—जर नुकसान नैसर्गिक आपत्ती/कीड-रोगामुळे पिकाची उत्पादनक्षमता घटली असेल तर विमा, आणि जर पुढील हंगामात नवीन लागवडीसाठी आधार हवा असेल तर क्षेत्रविस्तार योजना उपलब्ध आहे.

**प्रधानमंत्री पीक विमा योजना (पीएमएफबीवाय):**
ही केंद्र शासनाची योजना आहे जी नैसर्गिक आपत्ती, कीड व रोगामुळे होणाऱ्या पिकाच्या नुकसानात आर्थिक संरक्षण देते; इन्सिडेन्टी लेव्हल ७० टक्के निश्चित आहे.

**पात्रता:**
- अधिसूचित क्षेत्रातील अधिसूचित पिकांची लागवड करणारे सर्व शेतकरी
- कर्जदार व गैरकर्जदार दोघांसाठी ही योजना पर्यायी आहे

**अर्जासाठी कागदपत्रे:**
- आयस्टॅक क्रमांक
- आधार कार्ड
- बँक खाते तपशील
- जमीन व पीक तपशील
- डिजिटल पीक सर्वेक्षण (ई-पीक पाहणी)

**क्रिशोन्नती योजना – एकात्मिक बागायत विकास अभियान (एम.आय.डी.एच.) – क्षेत्रविस्तार (फळ, फुलगठ्ठा व मसाला पिके):**
ही केंद्र शासनाची योजना आहे जी फळ, फुलगठ्ठा व मसाला पिकांची नवीन लागवड करण्यासाठी सहाय्य देते.

**लाभ (निवडक पिके):**
- ड्रॅगन फ्रूट: खर्च मानक **₹६७५०००** प्रति हेक्टर; साधारण भागात अनुदान **₹२७००००** प्रति हेक्टर, अनुसूचित भागात **₹३३७५०००** प्रति हेक्टर
- आव्हाकॅडो: खर्च मानक **₹१२५०००** प्रति हेक्टर; साधारण भागात अनुदान **₹५००००** प्रति हेक्टर, अनुसूचित भागात **₹६२५०००** प्रति हेक्टर
- स्ट्रॉबेरी: खर्च मानक **₹२०००००** प्रति हेक्टर; साधारण भागात अनुदान **₹८००००** प्रति हेक्टर, अनुसूचित भागात **₹१०००००** प्रति हेक्टर

**पात्रता:**
- किमान ०.२० हेक्टर जमीन धारणा
- पूर्णपणे नवीन लागवड (पुर्वी लागवड केलेल्या क्षेत्रासाठी अनुदान नाही)

*Scheme Code*:
mahadbt-pmfby

*Sponsor*:
Central

*Scheme Provider*:
Maha-DBT

*Scheme Name*:
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

*Main Component*:
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)

*Sub Component*:
Risk covered -  Crop cutting base average yield reduction in comparison to threshhold yield for that insurance unit( Revenue circle)

*Introduction*:
1. The scheme is applicable for notified crops in a notified area (revenue circle). All farmers including share-croppers, tenant farmers growing notified crops in the notified area.
2. The scheme is optional for both loanee as well as non-loanee  farmers.
3. Under this scheme, the indemnity level is  fixed as 70 % for all notified crops.
4. Threshold yield  is determined by taking into account the average average yield  of the  best five years from past 7 years multiplied by  indemnity level
5. The scheme is implemented on beed pattern (80:110) where Insurance companies claim liability is up to 110 %  of the gross premium  or 110% of the burn cost whichever is higher for the given cluster in given season .  The claims above 110 % will be paid by state govt. and in case of profit, Insurance company will keep 20% of the gross premium and return the balance premium amount to state if any .

*Benefits*:
Provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of  crop failure due to natural calamaties, pests and disease so as to restore credit worthiness for ensuring season.

*Eligibility*:
1. All the farmers  growing notified crops in the notified area are eligible.
2. The scheme is  optional for Loanee & Non-loanee farmers.

Sum insured per hector: Sum insured per hectare is decided as per scale of finance for that crop

Insurance Companies: The scheme is being implemented through selected  crop insurance companies  through tendering process.

*Required Documents*:
1. Agristack number
2. Aadhar card
3. Bank account details
4. Land details and crop details
5. Digital crop survey ( E pik Pahani)

*Application Process*:
Application is to done online on www.pmfby.gov.in portal within the given date

Central

Maha-DBT

*Scheme Name*:
Krishonnati Yojana-
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)

*Main Component*:
Area Expansion

*Sub Component*:
Plantation of fruit, Flower & Spice crops

*Introduction*:
Under the Mission, assistance will be provided for Area Expansion by Plantation of fruit, Flower & Spices crops.
1. To Increase productivity by using high yielding varieties of fruit crops (Dragon fruit, Avocado & Strawberry) in the area expansion component.
2. To expand the area of ??non-traditional fruits, flowers outside greenhouses around major cities in the state.
3. To chectarenge traditional floriculture and use improved and high-yielding varieties for cultivation
4. Adopting high-tech cultivation methods for better quality production,

*Benefits*:
Benefit is given to farmers for 2 hectare area.
1. Dragon fruit - Benefit includes the cost of planting material, cost of material for trellis and other support systems, in 2 instalments of 60:40 subject to survival rate of 80% in 2nd year. Cost norms Rs. 6.75 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 2.70 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 3.375 lakh/hectare
2. Avocado - Benefit includes the cost of planting material and other input cost in 2
instalments of 60:40 subject to survival rate of 80% in 2nd year. Cost norms Rs. 1.25 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 0.50 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 0.625 lakh/hectare
3. Strawberry - Benefit includes the cost of on planting material and other input cost in one installment. Cost norms Rs. 2.00 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 0.80 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 1.00 lakh/hectare
4. Cut Flowers - Benefit is given in one installment. Cost norms Rs. 1.25 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 0.50 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 0.625 lakh/hectare
5. Bulbous and Rhizomatic Flowers -Benefit is given in one installment. Cost norms Rs. 2.50 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 1.00 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 1.25 lakh/hectare
6. Loose Flowers -Benefit is given in one installment. Cost norms Rs. 0.50 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 0.20 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 0.25 lakh/hectare
7. Chilli - Benefit includes the cost of planting material and cost of material for INM/IPM
etc. in one installment. Cost norms Rs. 0.50 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 0.20 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 0.25 lakh/hectare
8. Ginger & Turmeric - Benefit includes the cost on planting material and cost of material for INM/IPM etc. in one installment. Cost norms Rs. 1.00 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 0.40 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 0.50 lakh/hectare
9. Perennial Spices - Benefit includes the cost on planting material and cost of material for INM/IPM etc. in one installment. Cost norms Rs. 1.00 lakh/hectare, subsidy 40 % in General area is 0.40 lakh/hectare & 50 % in Scheduled area is 0.50 lakh/hectare

*Eligibility*:
1. To avail the benefit Farmers should hold at least 0.20 hectare land
2. Under this scheme, the cultivation of crops hectares to be done completely new. subsidy will not be payable for the area where crops were previously cultivated.

*Required Documents*:
1. Agristack Farmer ID
2. 7/12 and 8A (can be fetched through farmer ID)
3. Photocopy of the first page of the bank passbook (Aadhectarear linked Nationalised bank account details)
4. Caste certificate for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled tribes farmers
5. Consent letter if joint land holder
6. Guarantee letter in prescribed format
7. Bill/Invoice

question: वाशिम भागात माझ्या मूग पिकासाठी गोदाम शोधा.
answer:
वाशिम भागातील गोदामाची माहिती सध्या सिस्टममध्ये उपलब्ध नाही, पण तुमच्या नोंदणीकृत स्थानानुसार (लोहा–नांदेड) जवळची काही गोदामे खाली दिली आहेत.

**लोहा गोदाम**  
पत्ता: एमएसडब्ल्यूसी, एपीएमसी बाजार यार्ड, शिवाजी चौक, लोहा  
संपर्क: गोदाम व्यवस्थापक, फोन: ९०२८५२१३३२  
अंतर: १३.३६ कि.मी.

**नांदेड, एमआयडीसी गोदाम**  
पत्ता: एमएसडब्ल्यूसी, प्लॉट क्रमांक बी-१४, एमआयडीसी परिसर, नांदेड  
संपर्क: गोदाम व्यवस्थापक, फोन: ०२४६२-२२६५०७, ९१५८००१३३५  
अंतर: १७.२० कि.मी.

**पुरणा गोदाम**  
पत्ता: एमएसडब्ल्यूसी, नांदेड रोड, पुरणा  
संपर्क: गोदाम व्यवस्थापक, फोन: ०२४५२-२५५२१५, ९५४५०११६९३

question: पिक विमा योजनांचा अर्ज कसा करावा आणि कोणत्या पिकांसाठी आहे?
answer:
**पीक विमा योजना (पीएमएफबीवाय)** ही केंद्र सरकारची योजना आहे जी अधिसूचित क्षेत्रातील अधिसूचित पिकांसाठी हवामान अपघात, कीड व रोगमुळे पीक नुकसान झाल्यास आर्थिक संरक्षण देते; अर्ज दिला जाणारा तारखांच्या मर्यादेत **पीएमएफबीवाय डॉट गव्ह डॉट इन** पोर्टलवर ऑनलाईन करावा लागतो.

**कोणत्या पिकांसाठी:**
- अधिसूचित (नोटिफाइड) क्षेत्रात कोणते पीक विम्याखाली येते ते ठराविक (आवकाळ/कार्यालय) क्षेत्रानुसार बदलते; म्हणून तुमच्या वाशिम जिल्ह्यातील मालेगाव तालुक्यातील बोर्डी गाव परिसरात सध्या कोणती पिके अधिसूचित आहेत हे स्थानिक कार्यालय/अधिसूचनेनुसार खात्री करून घ्यावे.

**पात्रता:**
- अधिसूचित क्षेत्रात अधिसूचित पीक घेणारे सर्व शेतकरी, शेती भाडेकरू आणि लोनधारक किंवा बिगर लोनधारक (परव선택)
- महसूल मंडळ पातळीवर कार्यान्वित योजना

**अर्ज कसा करावा:**
- दिलेल्या तारखांच्या मर्यादेत **पीएमएफबीवाय डॉट गव्ह डॉट इन** पोर्टलवर ऑनलाईन अर्ज करावा लागतो.

**आवश्यक कागदपत्रे:**
- आधार कार्ड  
- बँक खाते तपशील  
- जमीन तपशील आणि पीक तपशील  
- डिजिटल पीक पाहणी (ई-पीक पाहणी)

**टीप:** योजनेचा लाभ हा त्या पिकाच्या निश्चित अनुदान मापदंडानुसार निर्धारित असतो.

**स्रोत: शासकीय योजना माहिती**?

तुम्हाला कोणत्या पिकासाठी विमा घ्यायचा आहे (उदा. हरभरा, सोयाबीन, मका, कापूस इ.)??

Risk covered -  Crop cutting base average yield reduction in comparison to threshhold yield for that insurance unit( Revenue circle)

*Introduction*:
1. The scheme is applicable for notified crops in a notified area (revenue circle). All farmers including share-croppers, tenant farmers growing notified crops in the notified area.
2. The scheme is optional for both loanee as well as non-loanee  farmers.
3. Under this scheme, the indemnity level is  fixed as 70 % for all notified crops.
4. Threshold yield  is determined by taking into account the average average yield  of the  best five years from past 7 years multiplied by  indemnity level
5. The scheme is implemented on beed pattern (80:110) where Insurance companies claim liability is up to 110 %  of the gross premium  or 110% of the burn cost whichever is higher for the given cluster in given season . Provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of  crop failure due to natural calamaties, pests and disease so as to restore credit worthiness for ensuring season.

*Eligibility*:

2. The scheme is  optional for Loanee & Non-loanee farmers.

3. Bank account details

- After 3 months, when sugarcane [ऊस] reaches a height of 4 feet, stop irrigating channel 1.
- For the next 3 months, irrigate only channel 3.
- Stop irrigation [सिंचन] in the remaining channels so that roots spread in search of water and become stronger.
- This helps to increase both the height and yield [उत्पादन] of sugarcane [ऊस].
- Using this method, about 40,000 healthy canes per acre can be obtained.

(v) Ratoon Crop [खोडवा पीक]

- After harvesting [कापणी] sugarcane [ऊस], allow the fallen leaves to dry [कोरडे].
- Then, move the dry [कोरडे] leaves from channel 2 into channel 4, and from channel 1 into channel 3.
- Ensure that sugarcane [ऊस] sets are not covered they should remain free for sprouting [अंकुरण].
- After this, sow [मादी डुक्कर] legume [शिंबीवर्गीय वनस्पती] seeds in channel 2 and channel 4 to improve crop yield [पीक उत्पादन].

(vi) Pest Management [कीड व्यवस्थापन]

- When needed, mix 3 litres *Brahmastra* and 3 litres *Agniastra* with 200 litres of water and spray.
- This mixture helps in controlling pests.

Vermicompost [गांडूळखत] is made from farm waste, plant-based materials, and cow dung [शेण] by earthworms. Vermicompost [गांडूळखत] contains various bacteria [जीवाणू], enzymes, vitamins [जीवनसत्त्वे], and other useful chemicals, which have a positive effect on plant growth [वाढ].

In the current situation, sustainable agriculture [शाश्वत शेती] is gaining importance as an alternative to chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते]. However, it is not possible to stop the use of chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते] immediately and replace them entirely with organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते]. This is because the large quantities of organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते] required are not readily available, and the possibility of a sudden decline in food production [उत्पादन] cannot be ruled out. Therefore, by using an integrated approach of chemical and organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते], and by maintaining the physical [शारीरिक तपासणी], chemical, and biological properties of the soil [माती] through the use of organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते], the balance of the environment can be maintained.

Therefore, it is necessary to implement measures to divert available organic matter [सेंद्रिय पदार्थ] towards agriculture [शेती], and in the current situation, it has become crucial for farmers to turn to organic farming [सेंद्रिय शेती]. It is necessary to prepare compost [कंपोस्ट] fertilizer [खत] and vermicompost [गांडूळखत] from the available crop [पीक] residues. The following methods are commonly used for their preparation.

**Method of Preparing Compost [कंपोस्ट] Fertilizer [खत]:** Crops absorb nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] from the soil [माती], so it is necessary to maintain soil fertility [मृदा सुपीकता]. Therefore, it is the need of the hour to prepare organic fertilizer [सेंद्रिय खत] from available waste and apply it to the soil [माती], that is, to return all the plant-based materials from the field [शेत] back to the field [शेत]. Organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते] increase the soil [माती]'s fertility [प्रजननक्षमता] and water retention [पाणी धारणक्षमता] capacity, provide nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] in the right amount, make the soil [माती] friable, and keep the air circulating. Because plants receive natural nutrients [पोषक तत्वे], their vigor increases, and it helps to promote the growth [वाढ] of beneficial microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव]. Fertilizer [खत] is not produced just by piling up crop residue [पीक अवशेष]. The following points must be followed for that:

**Location and Size of the Compost Pit [कंपोस्ट खड्डा]:** The location of the fertilizer [खत] pit should preferably be high and near the animal shed [निवारा]. The pit around the compost pit [कंपोस्ट खड्डा] should be about 10-15 cm high, as rainwater seeps into the pit and rots the waste. The decomposition of waste is carried out by microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव], and they require the necessary moisture and temperature [तापमान] for their growth [वाढ]. For that, water should be readily available as required. During the rainy season, rainwater should not enter the fertilizer [खत] pit, so a temporary roof (of turati/palanati) should be provided.

**Integrated Nutrient Management [एकात्मिक पोषण व्यवस्थापन] (INM):**

The method of using organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते], green manures, bacterial fertilizers, and organic [सेंद्रिय] liquids in appropriate proportions as complementary fertilizers along with chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते] is called Integrated Nutrient Management [एकात्मिक पोषण व्यवस्थापन].

In this method, a balance is maintained between chemical, organic [सेंद्रिय], and biological fertilizers [जैविक खत]. Also, by including leguminous crops [शेंगायुक्त पीक] in crop rotation [पीक फेरपालट], soil fertility [मृदा सुपीकता] is maintained. In this method, along with bumper crop [पीक] production [उत्पादन], the quality of food grains [धान्ये] and soil [माती] is also improved. By saving expensive chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते], soil productivity [मृदा उत्पादकता] is continuously improved year after year. In this method, generally half of the total requirement of nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] is supplied through chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते], and the remaining half is supplied through organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते]. It is recommended to take green manure crops [हिरवळीची खतपिके] and bury them in the soil [माती] once every three years. All crop [पीक] residues like sugarcane [ऊस] trash, sorghum [ज्वारी] stalks, wheat [गहू] and paddy stubble [खुंट], sunflower [सुर्यफुल] stalks, and all residues of pulse [डाळ] crops, etc., are buried in the soil [माती] to increase the amount of organic matter [सेंद्रिय पदार्थ]. Along with this, it is necessary to use bacterial fertilizers and vermicompost [गांडूळखत].

**The following points should be considered while selecting chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते]:**

1. For long-term crops, compound fertilizers should be used (Nitrophosphate 15:15:15) (Ammo. Phosphate 28:28:0).
2. To facilitate the availability of phosphorus [स्फुरद], completely soluble fertilizers should be selected. E.g., Single Super Phosphate, Diammonium Phosphate.
3. Sulfur-containing fertilizers should be included for pulses and oilseeds. E.g., Ammonium Sulfate, Single Super Phosphate, Ammo. Phosphate, Sulfate.
4. To increase the efficiency of phosphorus [स्फुरद], phosphorus [स्फुरद]-solubilizing bacteria [जीवाणू] (PSB) fertilizers should be used.
5. To increase the efficiency of nitrogenous fertilizers, coated urea [यूरिया] should be used. (Neem [कडूलिंब] Coated Urea [यूरिया], Sulfur Coated Urea [यूरिया].)
6. Glyricidia or young branches of Subabul [सुबाभळ] should be used as green manures.
7. Sugarcane [ऊस] molasses [मोलासेस] from sugar factories, bacterial fertilizers (Bio Earth Compost [कंपोस्ट]) should be used.

**Biopesticides for Eco-Friendly Pest Management by ICAR**
```
ix
INTRODUCTION
Pests and pathogens cause a major loss of agricultural produce every year. Management [व्यवस्थापन] of these menace using chemical pesticides [रासायनिक कीटकनाशके] and fungicides [बुरशीनाशके] has come at the cost of long term agricultural sustainability [कृषी टिकाऊपणा]. This non-judicious use of agrochemicals [कृषीरसायने] coupled with climate change [हवामान बदल] worsened the situation leading to changes in pest [कीड] and pathogen [रोगजनक] behaviour and development of resistance. Microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव] due to their extraordinary metabolic diversity are known to produce a battery of secondary metabolites including antimicrobial peptides, volatiles, toxins and enzymes [विषद्रव्ये व एंझाइम्स]. Many such microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव] have been substantially utilized as biopesticides [जैव कीटकनाशक] to control several phytopathogenic fungi, bacteria [जीवाणू], nematodes and insect [कीटक] pests. Unlike their chemical counter parts, biopesticides [जैव कीटकनाशक] aid to manage pests and pathogens without any adverse effects on soil health [मृदा आरोग्य] and environment. Microbial biopesticides [जैव कीटकनाशक] developed with microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव] like Trichoderma [ट्रायकोडर्मा], Beauveria, Metarhizium [मेटारिझियम], Bacillus, Pseudomonas [स्यूडोमोनास एक सामान्य संक्रामक जीव] are known for their role in management [व्यवस्थापन] of pests and pathogens. With the increasing reports on emerging pests and pathogens, the biopesticides [जैव कीटकनाशक] are expected to play a major role in sustainable management [व्यवस्थापन]. Currently, about 20 microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव] are registered as biopesticides [जैव कीटकनाशक] with Central Insecticide [कीटकनाशक] Board and Registration [नोंदणी] Committee (CIB & RC).
ICAR through its constituent institutes and All India Coordinated Research Projects (AICRPs) has developed and validated various formulations of biopesticides [जैव कीटकनाशक]. Challenges faced by biopesticides [जैव कीटकनाशक] are lower efficacy and shelf life [टिकाऊपणा], narrow host range, inability to reproduce the results under field [शेत] conditions. Constant efforts are being made by ICAR to overcome these challenges. **Animal Health and Nutrition Extension**
```
Impact of livestock [पशुधन] on soil [माती] and water

The high density of animals in confined areas leads to the deposition of significant amounts of nitrogen [नत्र], phosphorus [स्फुरद], organic matter [सेंद्रिय पदार्थ] and faecal microbes in watersheds (Mallin *et al*., 2015). This, in turn, contaminates water systems globally, contributing to issues like surface water eutrophication [पोषणतत्त्व अधिकता] (nutrient [पोषक घटक] enrichment causing excessive plant and algae growth [वाढ]) and groundwater nitrate enrichment. Livestock waste [पशुधन कचरा] contains high levels of organic matter [सेंद्रिय पदार्थ], suspended solids, nutrients [पोषक तत्वे], metals, and pharmaceutical compounds. Unbalanced application of livestock manure [पशुधन खत] on soil [माती] can result in the leaching [झिरपण प्रक्रिया] of nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] and antibiotics into ground and surface waters, negatively impacting water quality [पाण्याची गुणवत्ता]. This can lead to the growth [वाढ] of algae, acceleration of eutrophication [पोषणतत्त्व अधिकता], and the spread of antibiotic [प्रतिजैविक]-resistant bacteria [जीवाणू] (Almeida *et al*., 2017). To address these issues, the European Community implemented the Nitrates Directive in 1991 (Directive 91/676/EEC). This directive aims to reduce water pollution [जल प्रदूषण] caused by nitrates from agricultural sources by setting strict concentration limits for nitrates in both surface and ground water. Livestock [पशुधन] inadequately utilize phosphorus [स्फुरद], with 60 to 80% of consumed phosphorus [स्फुरद] being excreted. When applied to the land, phosphorus [स्फुरद] tends to accumulate in the soil [माती]. Only a small percentage (320%) may reach water bodies through runoff [वाहून जाणारे पाणी] or leaching [झिरपण प्रक्रिया] processes. Excessive phosphorus [स्फुरद] in waterways contributes to nutrient [पोषक घटक] enrichment and the potential for eutrophication [पोषणतत्त्व अधिकता]. The concentration of animals in confined spaces leads to the deposition of pollutants in watersheds, resulting in water contamination and contributing to issues such as eutrophication [पोषणतत्त्व अधिकता]. Effective management [व्यवस्थापन] practices, regulations, and sustainable agricultural approaches are crucial to mitigate the environmental impact [पर्यावरणीय परिणाम] of livestock farming [पशुपालन] on water quality [पाण्याची गुणवत्ता].

question: मी माझ्या शेतासाठी केंद्रातून सौर-ऊर्जा पंप भाड्याने घेऊ शकतो का?
answer:
तुमच्या सध्याच्या प्रोफाइलनुसार तुमचे गाव पोक्रा-नियुक्त नाही, त्यामुळे केंद्राकडून थेट सौर पंप भाड्याने देण्याची योजना तुम्हाला लागू होणार नाही.

**पर्याय (योजना):** **उप-अभियान कृषी यांत्रिकीकरण** ही केंद्र योजना आहे जी अनुबंध भाड्यासाठी केंद्र (सीएचसी) स्थापनेस ४०% अनुदान देते; त्यात शेतकी यंत्रसामग्री बँक/सीएचसी आणि किसान ड्रोन अशी घटकही दिलेली आहेत.  
**पात्रता:**

*Scheme Code*:

*Sponsor*:
Central

*Scheme Provider*:
DDA MECHANIZATION

*Scheme Name*:
Sub-Mission on Agriculture Mechanization

*Main Component*:
Benefit for Custom Hiring Centre

*Sub Component*:
1. Farm Machinery Banks
2. Kisan Drone

*Introduction*:
The declining number of livestock and the shortage of labor for agricultural work necessitate mechanization in agriculture. Mechanization allows work to be completed within a specified time frame, saves inputs, and saves production costs.
Objective:-
        Resolve labour issues in agriculture.
        Promote Farm Mechanization.
        Enable farmers to take up farm operations in time.
        Promote custom hiring services for farm mechanization.
        Create rural employment.
        Help to Increase agriculture production.

*Benefits*:
1. A subsidy of 40% of the capital cost is provided for the establishment of an Farm Machinery Bank/Custom Hiring Centre (CHC)

2. Subsidy of 50% of the total expenditure for agriculture graduates or maximum rs. 5.00 lakh and Subsidy of 40% of the expenditure for other beneficiaries or upto maximum limit 4.00 lakh, whichever is lower for kisan drones.

*Eligibility*:
1. Indiviual beneficiary, Farmer Groups, Women Self Help Groups, Farmer Producer Company, Farmer co-operative society, Primary Agriculture Co-operative credit society.

*Required Documents*:
1. Quotation of Implement to be purchase.
2. Test report of the Implement.
3. RC of tractor for tractor driven implements.
4. Registration Certificate for farmer producer company or farmer groups.

*Application Process*:
Applications from Interested farmers are invited on https://mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in/ this portal. For transparency in beneficiary selection, presanction is being given by determining seniority through FCFS method. All the processes from beneficiary selection to grant payment are being implemented online.
After presanction, farmers are being allowed to purchase from the open market as per their choice. At the time of purchase, farmers are required to make payment through cheque/DD/online from their own bank account. The subsidy amount is being transferred to the Aadhaar-linked bank account of the beneficiary farmer through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) method.

नाशिक जिल्ह्यात खालील गोदामांमध्ये संपर्क करून ५० क्विंटल द्राक्षांसाठी जागा उपलब्ध आहे की नाही ते थेट विचारू शकता; मात्र सध्याच्या माहितीत कोणत्या गोदामात नेमकी किती जागा रिकामी आहे याचा अद्ययावत तपशील दिसत नाही.

अंतर: १४.६ कि.मी.

question: ठिबक सिंचनाद्वारे सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये देण्याची सर्वोत्तम पद्धत कोणती?
answer:
ठिबक सिंचनाद्वारे सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये देण्याची सर्वात योग्य पद्धत म्हणजे पाण्यात पूर्णपणे विरघळणारी (पाणी-विद्राव्य) सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्य खते निश्चित मात्रेत ठिबकातून मुळांच्या भागात देणे, आणि एकूण कार्यक्षमता वाढीसाठी आवश्यक तेवढी फवारणीही करणे.

**सिंचनाद्वारे खत देणे:** ठिबक सिंचनाने पाणी व खत/अन्नद्रव्ये एकत्र देण्याच्या या पद्धतीला सिंचनाद्वारे खत देणे असे म्हणतात; यामध्ये खत टाकी, व्हेंच्युरी किंवा इंजेक्शन पंप सारखी साधने वापरली जातात आणि खत पाण्यात नीट मिसळले जाऊन वरील नळीद्वारे धारायुक्त झाल्यावर प्रणालीत घुसते व ठिबकातून मुळांच्या परिसरात सोडले जाते.

**सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये:** उपलब्ध दस्तऐवजांतून सरकारी-मान्य पाणी-विद्राव्य खतांची यादी दिलेली आहे, तसेच ऊसासाठी ठिबकाद्वारे खत देण्याचा उदाहरणार्थी प्रयोग हा चार समान हप्त्यांत देण्याचे दिलेले आहे: लागवडीवेळी, ६० दिवसांनी, १२० दिवसांनी आणि १८० दिवसांनी.

**फवारणी (पूरक):** सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये गरजेनुसार पानांवर फवारणीने द्यावीत अशी शिफारसही दिलेली आहे; उदाहरणार्थ, भेंडीमध्ये सिट्रिक ऍसिड आधारित स्तर द्वितीय सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये पानांवर फवारणीने प्रति लीटर पाणी दहा मि.ली. (१%) याप्रमाणे देण्याची शिफारस दिलेली आहे.

**टीप:** स्रोत दस्तऐवजांतून ठिबकाद्वारे कोणती सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये, त्यांची अचूक प्रति एकर मात्रा, किंवा कोणत्या पिकासाठी नेमके वेळापत्रक हे सर्व सविस्तर माहिती उपलब्ध नाही; पण वरील पद्धत व उदाहरणार्थी वेळापत्रक/मात्रा ही उपलब्ध माहिती असल्यामुळे तीच सध्या मार्गदर्शक मानू शकता.

**स्रोत: कृषी एन.पी.के. माहिती (कृषी विद्यापीठ दस्तऐवज), एम.पी.केव्ही संशोधन शिफारसी २०२३ राहुरी, डॉ. पंजाबराव देशमुख कृषी विद्यापीठ**

Fertigation [सिंचनाद्वारे खत देणे] is the process of giving fertilizers to crops in liquid form or soluble in water through micro irrigation [सूक्ष्म सिंचन] or drip irrigation system [ठिबक सिंचन प्रणाली]. For delivering soluble fertilizers to crops through micro irrigation [सूक्ष्म सिंचन] systems, fertilizer [खत] tanks, venture, and injection pumps etc. are mainly used.

**Venturi:** The venturi is a dumb-bell shaped device with a decreasing diameter in the middle, which increases the flow rate of water and reduces the available pressure in the middle of the venture, allowing the fertilizer [खत] to be available through the manifold during irrigation [सिंचन]. Given on the ground through drips. The water in the fertilizer tank [खत साठवण टाकी] should be mixed and then the pipe coming out of that tank should be left in the venturi. After starting the drip irrigation system [ठिबक सिंचन प्रणाली], if both the control valves are started, the fertilizers from the tank are absorbed/drawn through the venturi and mixed with the water flow in the pipe of the system and released through the dripper on the manifold or in the area of the roots of the trees/crops.

*ii) Micro minerals [खनिजे] (minor minerals [खनिजे] or trace minerals [सूक्ष्म खनिज]):* Required in trace amounts (<100 mg per day) and are expressed in terms of part per million (PPM) or mg/kg diet. The important trace elements [सूक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये] are iron [लोह], copper [तांबे], iodine [आयोडिन], cobalt, manganese [मॅंगनीज], zinc [झिंक], fluorine, selenium, molybdenum [मॉलिब्डेनम], chromium, nickel, silicon, tin, and vanadium

**Measures for Vegetable Crops in Drought [दुष्काळ] Conditions**

In drought [दुष्काळ] conditions, good market prices are obtained for vegetable crops and farmers get good benefits as vegetable cultivation is very limited due to adverse climate [हवामान] (high temperature [तापमान] and dry [कोरडे] hot air) and water scarcity [पाण्याची कमतरता]. For this, it is important to select the right vegetable crop [पीक] and get quality production [उत्पादन] from it. It is difficult to grow vegetable crops in drought [दुष्काळ] conditions, but some measures can be taken to use less water, e.g. to cultivate some vegetables by using drip and sprinkler irrigation [तुषार सिंचन]. Some important measures for this are as follows.

1. Selecting vegetable crops that require less water e.g. drumstick, hadga, guar and leafy vegetables.
2. Use of soil [माती] cover.
3. Onion [कांदा] Nursery [रोपवाटिका] Management [व्यवस्थापन].

- Onion [कांदा] crop [पीक] nursery [रोपवाटिका] should be prepared on raised beds [उंच केलेले वाफे].
- Seed treatment [बीज प्रक्रिया] should be done before sowing [पेरणी] onion [कांदा] seeds.
- Do not use too much chemical fertilizer [रासायनिक खत] on raised beds [उंच केलेले वाफे].
- Water the nursery [रोपवाटिका] before sowing [पेरणी] the seeds and sow [मादी डुक्कर] the seeds.
- Sow [मादी डुक्कर] the seeds thinly and then use a sprinkler [तुषार सिंचन] or rain gun.
- Use shed [निवारा] net on the nursery [रोपवाटिका] if possible.

1. To protect against dry [कोरडे] and hot winds, drumstick crop [पीक] or dense planting of maize [मका] should be done on all four sides of the field [शेत] or around the wind [वारा].
2. Water management [पाण्याचे व्यवस्थापन] through micro irrigation [सूक्ष्म सिंचन] methods (drip or sprinkler [तुषार सिंचन]).
3. Proper balance of chemical and organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते].
4. Selecting varieties with more leaves and protecting flowers and fruits from heat through them.

7. To reduce the intensity of heat, use a porous plastic mesh (shed [निवारा] net).
8. Proper use of available water - especially ensure even water supply during flowering to fruit harvesting [कापणी] period and that too in the morning, morning or evening and at night (avoid watering in the hot sun).
9. Harvest [कापणी] the fruits preferably in the evening and transport the goods (in the morning) after grading [गटवारी] packaging [पॅकेजिंग].

Economic and environmental considerations

Dietary requirement of minerals [खनिजे] will be greatly reduced by the addition of organic [सेंद्रिय] minerals [खनिजे] to animal diets, but cost-to-benefit ratio [प्रमाण] need to be considered. More often in comparative studies using organic [सेंद्रिय] and inorganic sources, the cost is calculated as one to one basis. But one should keep in mind that if inorganic elements are 40-50% bioavailable, chelated minerals [खनिजे] are 2-2.5 times more bioavailable. Due environmental concerns, it becomes necessary to lower supplemental trace mineral levels and adjust proportions of inorganic with organic [सेंद्रिय] in order to maintain optimum performance, profitability [फायदेशीरता] and environmental stability.

Similar to trace mineral bioavailability [जैवउपलब्धता], issue of phosphorus [स्फुरद] (P) in monogastrics is a concern. A multifaceted approach integrating nutrition [पोषण], genetics, manure management [खत व्यवस्थापन] and innovative soil [माती] and crop management practices [पीक व्यवस्थापन पद्धती] is required to lower faecal- P excretion. Reducing dietary P inputs through judicious use of feedstuffs and improving gut utilization of P to reduce faecal-P excretion. Desired dietary level of P in ruminant [गुरे वर्ग] and monogastric animals and improving gut bioavailability [जैवउपलब्धता] using better bioavailable inorganic sources and balancing of different micronutrients [सुक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये] and phytase enzyme supplementation are few of the remedies. question: फक्त सांगत नाहीत, तर करून दाखवणारी व्यवस्था आहे का?
answer:

  फोन: ९५२७०५८२६८

question: माझ्या गावात गेल्या ३ दिवसांत पिकाच्या वाढीसाठी पुरेसा सूर्यप्रकाश मिळाला का?
answer:
जवळा (दे) (तालुका लोहा, जिल्हा नांदेड) साठी गेल्या ३ दिवसांत पाऊस झाला नाही आणि तापमान उष्ण राहिले आहे; पण या हवामान इतिहास डेटामध्ये प्रत्यक्ष सूर्यप्रकाशाच्या तासांची नोंद दिलेली नाही.

**गेल्या ३ दिवसांचे हवामान:**
- १२ मार्च: पाऊस ० मिमी, किमान तापमान १८.०२ °से., कमाल तापमान ३७.२१ °से., सरासरी आर्द्रता ६७.८८ %
- १३ मार्च: पाऊस ० मिमी, किमान तापमान १८.१२ °से., कमाल तापमान ३९.०५ °से., सरासरी आर्द्रता ६३.१७ %
- १४ मार्च: पाऊस ० मिमी, किमान तापमान १९.३९ °से., कमाल तापमान ३८.३४ °से., सरासरी आर्द्रता ५७.४१ %

**आठवणीला येण्यासारखे मुद्दे:**

Water required for the crop [पीक] (liter/day/tree) = a x b x c x d

a = Evaporation of water from the soil [माती] (mm/day) b = Crop coefficient [पीक गुणांक]

c = Irrigation [सिंचन] coefficient d = Area covered by trees (sq. meters, m X m)

The information of the various components used in the above formula should be extracted as follows.

Evaporation of water from the soil [माती] (a): The water requirement of the crop [पीक] depends on the climate [हवामान] i.e. various components of the climate [हवामान] (e.g. temperature [तापमान], humidity [आर्द्रता], wind [वारा] speed, hours of sunshine per day, etc.). Information on evaporation of water can be obtained from the Meteorological Department's observatory or through an evaporation pan [बाष्पीभवन पॅन]. If farmers install an evaporation pan [बाष्पीभवन पॅन] collectively for the entire area, they can measure the evaporation of water through it. Evaporation from the soil [माती] is 70 to 80 percent of the evaporation from the evaporation pan [बाष्पीभवन पॅन]. For that, the evaporation pan [बाष्पीभवन पॅन] coefficient should be taken as 0.7 to 0.8. For Western Maharashtra, this coefficient should be taken as 0.8. If information on various components of the climate [हवामान] is available from the observatory, then the reference evaporation of water can also be extracted through the 'Phule Jal' computer program developed by this University.

Crop Coefficient [पीक गुणांक] (b): The water requirement varies according to the growth [वाढ] stage of the crops. The requirement is less in the initial stages. As the growth [वाढ] increases, the requirement increases and decreases slightly after full growth [वाढ] and flowering, fruiting. The changing water requirement according to crop [पीक] and crop [पीक] stage can be taken into account with the help of crop coefficient [पीक गुणांक]. The crop coefficient [पीक गुणांक] is usually between 0.2 and 1.15 according to the crop [पीक] and the stage of crop [पीक] growth [वाढ].

Thermal stress [तापमान ताण]

As ambient temperature [तापमान] and relative humidity [सापेक्ष आर्द्रता] rise, maintaining stable body temperature [शरीराचा तापमान] through heat dissipation mechanisms can become challenging, leading animals to experience heat stress [उष्णतेचा ताण]. This stress manifests in decreased dry matter [सुका घटक] intake, reduced milk yield [दुधाचे उत्पादन], and impaired reproductive performance, affecting overall production [उत्पादन]. Housing [निवास व्यवस्था] factors such as ventilation [हवेची आदळ], cooling, flooring, animal density, and regrouping influence the severity of stress, with deficiencies exacerbating seasonal stress. These multiple stressors can reduce growth [वाढ], production [उत्पादन], and reproductive potential by redistributing nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] to vital functions. Deviations from the thermoneutral zone trigger adaptive responses to restore thermal balance, altering welfare and growth [वाढ]. Animals employ physiological, molecular, endocrine, biochemical, and behavioural adaptations to maintain homeostasis, regulating variables like respiration [श्वसन] rate, pulse [डाळ] rate, and body temperature [शरीराचा तापमान]. Climatic stressors affect metabolism, altering enzymatic reactions, biochemical profiles, and blood [रक्त] metabolites. Elevated temperatures impact the hypothalamic appetite [भूक] centre, intestinal function, and metabolic pathways, leading to reduced growth [वाढ]. Heat stress [उष्णतेचा ताण] also adversely affects reproductive organs, including the anterior pituitary, pre-ovulatory follicles, corpus luteum, and embryo [भ्रूण] development, resulting in decreased fertility [प्रजननक्षमता] and increased foetal loss.

**Soluble Fertilizers:** The nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] supplied to the crop [पीक] from the chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते] applied through the soil [माती] are not fully available to the crop [पीक]. If the moisture in the soil [माती] is too high or too low, the nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] supplied from such fertilizers are not available to the crop [पीक]. In such adverse conditions, the stress of water and nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] on the crops has an adverse effect on crop nutrition [पीक पोषण] and growth [वाढ]. Apart from this, this availability also depends on soil [माती] properties such as soil temperature [मृद तापमान], pH, lime [चुना] content, organic carbon [सेंद्रिय कार्बन], etc. The amount of nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] that the crop [पीक] receives from the total nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] in the fertilizers we apply through the soil [माती] is called the efficiency of the fertilizers or nutrients [पोषक तत्वे]. In changing climatic conditions, especially in rainfed conditions, if there is prolonged heavy rainfall or drought [दुष्काळ], deficiency symptoms [लक्षणे] of nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] start appearing on the crop [पीक] through fertilizers applied from the soil [माती]. The growth [वाढ] of the crop [पीक] stops in a specific way and the yield [उत्पादन] decreases. In such a situation, fertilizers cannot be given from the soil [माती] and even if they are given, there is a possibility that they will not benefit the crop [पीक].

Soluble fertilizers are available in solid as well as liquid form. Solid fertilizers are 100% easily soluble in water and a solution suitable for use is prepared by mixing the required amount in water. If symptoms [लक्षणे] of nutrient deficiency [पोषण कमतरता] appear in the crops according to the growth [वाढ] stage of the crops or if the relevant soluble fertilizers are sprayed as per the recommendation as per the requirement, these fertilizers become available to the crops quickly and work effectively. # 3. BMP-2: Monitor and maintain the water temperature [तापमान] of production [उत्पादन] and fish [मासे] keeping facility within optimum range
Fish [मासे] are cold blooded i.e. poikilothermic animals, the body temperature [शरीराचा तापमान] of which changes according to that of environment, affecting its metabolism & physiology and ultimately the growth [वाढ], reproduction and production [उत्पादन]. A higher temperature [तापमान] increases the metabolic rate of fish [मासे] along with oxygen demand. It further causes decreased solubility of oxygen and also increased level of ammonia in water.
## Guiding factors for BMP-2
### 3.1 Find out optimum temperature tolerance [तापमानास सहनशील] range of species [प्रजाती] to be cultured
Fish [मासे] are generally characterised as warm water species [प्रजाती] (25-30^ ), cool water species [प्रजाती] (15-25^ ) and cold water [थंड पाणी] species [प्रजाती] ( 15^ ). Most of the freshwater ornamental species [प्रजाती] are under first two categories with an optimum value of 24-28^ . The growth [वाढ] of fish [मासे] increases with increase in temperature [तापमान] till some defined level, thereafter it decreases and leads to stress conditions followed by mortality. An increased temperature [तापमान] also decreases solubility of gases in water that leads to lower dissolved oxygen [विरघळलेले ऑक्सिजन] which is an added effect of thermal stress [तापमान ताण]. All these conditions result in poor growth [वाढ], continuous stress & even death under severe conditions. Hence, it is important to find out the temperature tolerance [तापमानास सहनशील] range of fishes that are being cultured.
### 3.2 Protecting fish [मासे] from temperature [तापमान] variations due to environmental change
Most of the ornamental fish [सजावटी माशा] breeding [प्रजनन] farms are located in coastal regions where both air and water temperatures remain same throughout the year

**Multi-Cropping System [पीक प्रणाली]:**

Multi-cropping system [पीक प्रणाली] means taking two or more crops from the same soil [माती] in the same year. In irrigated areas, crops are taken in all three seasons of the year. Two crops are taken only when water is available in Rabi season [रबी हंगाम].

The following factors are important to consider while selecting multi-cropping systems

1. Various varieties of crops and their maturity period.
2. The available varieties should be short-term maturing and high yielding, timely sowing [पेरणी] and number of plants, etc.
3. The varieties should respond well to fertilizers.
4. Farmyard manure [शेणखत], compost [कंपोस्ट] manure [खत], cakes, green manures should be used.
5. Bacterial culture such as Rhizobium [रायझोबियम], phosphorus [स्फुरद]-solubilizing bacteria [जीवाणू], Acetobacter, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, blue-green algae [निळा-हिरवा शैवाल] (B.G.A.) should be used for seed treatment [बीज प्रक्रिया] or for application through soil [माती].
6. The available Pala Pachola (Leaf Litter [कचरा]) and other residues in the field [शेत] should be mixed in the soil [माती] so that it helps to increase the soil texture [जमीनीचा पोत] and the amount of organic carbon [सेंद्रिय कार्बन].
7. Micronutrients [सुक्ष्म अन्नद्रव्ये] should be used. E.g., Zinc [झिंक], Iron [लोह], Molybdenum [मॉलिब्डेनम], Boron [बोरॉन], Manganese [मॅंगनीज], Copper [तांबे] etc.
8. In multi-cropping systems, micronutrient [सूक्ष्म मूलद्रव्ये] deficiencies are observed in crops. E.g., Molybdenum [मॉलिब्डेनम], Boron [बोरॉन], Sulfur etc.
9. There is a high possibility of infestation of noxious weeds [तण] in multi-cropping system [पीक प्रणाली]. E.g. Harali, Nagarmotha, Chandvel, Pathari. etc.

**Chain Cropping System [पीक प्रणाली]:**

When a second crop [पीक] is sown in the field [शेत] before or near harvesting [कापणी] of the first crop [पीक], such a cropping system [पीक प्रणाली] is called a chain cropping system [पीक प्रणाली]. In this method, the moisture that is in the first crop [पीक] benefits the second crop [पीक].

Benefits of Chain Cropping System [पीक प्रणाली]: -

1. The moisture that is in the first crop [पीक] benefits the second crop [पीक].
2. If you have water facility, the second crop [पीक] can be planted on time.
3. The duration of the second crop [पीक] is short.

The following cropping systems have been recommended for the Marathwada division [विभाग] as per the type of soil [माती].
